title: White Declines (2.Nc3, 2.e5, 2.d4, 2.Nf3)
intro: Seize the centre with 2...d4 against 2.Nc3, play 2...c5 against 2.e5, and take on e4 against the Blackmar-Diemer (2.d4) and Tennison (2.Nf3) gambits.
variation: e2e4 d7d5 b1c3, e2e4 d7d5 e4e5, e2e4 d7d5 d2d4, e2e4 d7d5 g1f3

lessons.title: Meeting 2.Nc3
lessons.summary: Gain space with 2...d4 and take over the centre with 3...e5.

steps.text: Instead of taking on d5, White sometimes guards e4 with 2.Nc3.
Gain space in the centre and chase the knight immediately.
steps.hint: Push your d-pawn forward to attack c3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...d4 so White must retreat the knight.
steps.ifRight: White's knight is driven backwards right away.

steps.text: White retreats to e2 with 3.Nce2, blocking the f1 bishop.
Claim the centre while White's pieces are tangled up.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...e5 to gain central space and lock in White's pieces.
steps.ifRight: Black already enjoys extra space and smooth development.

steps.text: White moves the knight again to g3: 4.Ng3.
Develop an active piece and stop Bc4 ideas.
steps.hint: Develop your light-squared bishop to e6 or knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Be6 (or 4...Nc6 or 4...Nf6) to control key dark squares.

lessons.title: Meeting 2.e5
lessons.summary: Strike at once with 2...c5 and bring your c8 bishop out actively.

steps.text: If White pushes past with 2.e5, the position looks like a French Defence, with one huge bonus for Black.
Strike at the centre right away before playing ...e6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2...c5: unlike the French, your c8 bishop is still free to come out to f5 or g4.
steps.ifRight: You get an improved French where your light-squared bishop is never trapped.

feedback.e7e6: 2...e6 shuts in your c8 bishop. Play 2...c5 first so your bishop can come out.

steps.text: Develop your queen's knight to control d4 and e5.
steps.hint: Bring the b8 knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Nc6 to pressure d4 and e5.

steps.text: White supports e5 with 4.d4. Put pressure on d4 or get your c8 bishop out.
steps.hint: Take on d4 first or bring your bishop to f5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...cxd4 (followed by ...Bf5 or ...Bg4) to attack White's centre.
steps.ifRight: After 4...cxd4 5.cxd4 Bf5, Black has an ideal position.

feedback.c8g4: With no knight on f3 there is nothing to pin, and the bishop gets into trouble. Take on d4 or go to f5.

steps.text: Here White played 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.c3. Bring your light-squared bishop out actively with a pin.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Bg4 to pin the knight and follow with ...e6.
steps.ifRight: With the bishop outside the pawn chain, Black plays ...e6 and ...Nge7 smoothly.

lessons.title: Meeting 2.d4 and 2.Nf3
lessons.summary: Accept the Blackmar-Diemer and Tennison gambits and develop your c8 bishop actively.

steps.text: In the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit, White plays 2.d4, offering the e4 pawn for open lines.

steps.ifRight: Now Black develops solidly and keeps the extra pawn.

steps.text: White offers a second pawn with 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3.
Take on f3 and keep your pieces active.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...exf3: after 5.Nxf3, bring your c8 bishop out to f5 or g4 before playing ...e6.
steps.ifRight: After 5.Nxf3 Bf5 (or 5...Bg4), Black stays a sound pawn up.

steps.text: Against 2.Nf3 dxe4, club players often try the tricky Tennison Gambit with 3.Ng5.
Defend your extra pawn while developing a piece.
steps.hint: Bring your c8 bishop to f5 to guard e4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Bf5 (followed by ...Nf6 and ...e6): you hold onto the extra pawn and stay rock solid.
steps.ifRight: After 4.Nc3 Nf6, Black protects e4 cleanly and keeps the extra pawn.
